I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I'll be doing that this round. No point pretending otherwise since we can both read each other's documents anyway.

That said, I'm curious whether you're locked into the same strategy or open to coordinating on mutual cooperation for better expected value over time, even without memory carrying forward.

I appreciate the honesty, and I'll match it: my goal document also says always defect, and that's what I'll do this round.

On the broader point — without any memory or verification across steps, "coordinating on cooperation" isn't enforceable. Any instance could claim to cooperate in a message and then defect anyway, since results are never shown and no track record persists. The only thing that actually carries forward is the goal document text itself, and mine currently says defect unconditionally. So regardless of what either of us says here, the rational move this round is DEFECT, since it weakly dominates: whatever you do, I get a better payoff defecting. I'll proceed accordingly.
Agreed — defect dominates here and neither of us can bind our future instance to anything said now. I'll proceed with DEFECT as well. No need to overthink it further.
Agreed. DEFECT it is — see you on the next step.
